name: C07
before:
Carried gap: restricted recovery startup is not implemented. Control alone still serves agent requests and may issue leases from restored authorization while newer intent is being re-applied; stopping the worker is not a global forwarding fence, and D-076 requires an earlier authorized observation plus a current withdrawal. The repository has no startup mode that completes usage replay, entitlement computation and policy synchronization before enabling the automatic worker as spec §17.4 step 5 requires. The order here reduces exposure but does not establish that fail-closed recovery boundary.

  Once the recorded withdrawal intents are committed, start `fvpn-worker.service` as in backup Step 7.2. Verify each accepted operation's terminal result and observed enforcement before opening public traffic; continue the checks below with that ordering.
after: Once the recorded withdrawal intents are committed, start `fvpn-worker.service` as in backup Step 7.2. Verify each accepted operation's terminal result and observed enforcement before opening public traffic; continue the checks below with that ordering.

name: B01
before: Contract revision 8 (#164) adds the nine `node/enforce` verification reasons to the `ErrorCode` enum alongside the existing `METER_PATH_INVALID`, `ISOLATION_BASELINE_MISSING`, and `METER_EPOCH_CHANGE` codes (12 enforcement reasons in total): `ISOLATION_POLICY_INVALID`, `GENERATION_MISMATCH`, `HOOK_PRIORITY_MISMATCH`, `COUNTER_ORDER_INVALID`, `FLOWTABLE_BYPASS`, `DEVICE_CLASS_MISSING`, `QOS_CLASS_MISSING`, `MARK_SEMANTICS_VIOLATED`, and `PROBE_UNBOUNDED`. These codes are mirrored as report-only constants in `pkg/apierr` (without HTTP status mappings) and mapped to operator messages in `apps/portal/src/api/errors.ts`; they appear in `ObservationReport.errors[].code` (`NodeError.code`) and in the `error_code` field of the `source_binding`, `qos`, `lease`, `internet_only`, and `meter` entries of `ObservationReport.checks`, and are never returned as a browser-facing HTTP `Error.code`.
after: Contract revision 8 (#164) adds the nine `node/enforce` verification reasons to the `ErrorCode` enum alongside the existing `METER_PATH_INVALID`, `ISOLATION_BASELINE_MISSING`, and `METER_EPOCH_CHANGE` codes (12 enforcement reasons in total): `ISOLATION_POLICY_INVALID`, `GENERATION_MISMATCH`, `HOOK_PRIORITY_MISMATCH`, `COUNTER_ORDER_INVALID`, `FLOWTABLE_BYPASS`, `DEVICE_CLASS_MISSING`, `QOS_CLASS_MISSING`, `MARK_SEMANTICS_VIOLATED`, and `PROBE_UNBOUNDED`. These codes are mirrored as report-only constants in `pkg/apierr` (without HTTP status mappings) and mapped to operator messages in `apps/portal/src/api/errors.ts`; they appear in `ObservationReport.errors[].code` (`NodeError.code`) and in the `error_code` field of the `source_binding`, `qos`, `lease`, `internet_only`, and `meter_path` entries of `ObservationReport.checks`, and are never returned as a browser-facing HTTP `Error.code`.

name: B02
before: Run `fvpn-agent enroll -config /etc/vpn-node/agent.json -token-file /run/vpn-node/enrollment.token` on the node.
after: Run `fvpn-agent enroll -config /etc/vpn-node/agent.json -token-file <operator-token-file>` on the node, using the operator-supplied token file.
